title: Runtime instrumentation: standardize KV cache + batch efficiency metrics for cost model inputs
creator: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Context
- Standard Cost Model v1 requires runtime-exported inputs that are consistent across hosted/dedicated/private so Console + Optimize can rely on the same primitives.
- Today KV cache / prefix-cache stats and “batch efficiency” are either missing, inconsistently named, or not comparable across execution paths (continuous batching vs static, paged KV vs non-paged, quant kernels).
- This ticket adds + standardizes the runtime metrics contract so Telemetry can ingest a single shape and Cost Model can compute:
  - prefill vs decode attribution
  - cache hit/miss effects (token-attributable)
  - batch efficiency / queueing overhead indicators

Problem
- We cannot accurately explain cost deltas for:
  - prefix/KV cache hits (reused compute avoided)
  - changes in batching (batch size distribution, effective utilization)
  - differences in prefill vs decode cost weights
- Metrics exist in ad-hoc logs for some runtimes, but not as a stable contract with consistent units.

Goals (v1)
1) Emit request-level token accounting split by stage (prefill vs decode).
2) Emit KV cache effectiveness signals in token-equivalent units (so cost model can treat “saved work” consistently).
3) Emit batch efficiency signals with bounded cardinality (no per-layer/per-head breakdown).
4) Provide a backwards-compatible rollout path (dual-write + canary) and validation checks.

Non-goals (this ticket)
- Adding per-layer attention-kernel counters.
- Emitting detailed memory residency timelines.
- Replacing existing billing metering (we only provide inputs; billing alignment tracked separately).

Proposed metrics (contract)
NOTE: Exact field names must match ENG-4823 telemetry contracts once finalized. Below is proposed runtime-side naming; Telemetry team will map/normalize if needed.

A) Request token accounting (required)
- runtime.tokens.prefill.input_total
  - Definition: number of prompt tokens processed in prefill stage for this request (after normalization/tokenization as done by runtime)
  - Unit: tokens (int)
- runtime.tokens.decode.output_total
  - Definition: number of tokens generated in decode stage for this request
  - Unit: tokens (int)
- runtime.tokens.decode.steps_total
  - Definition: number of decode steps executed (should equal output_total for standard sampling; may differ for speculative/other paths)
  - Unit: steps (int)
- runtime.tokens.total = prefill.input_total + decode.output_total (derived, not required as a separate metric)

B) KV cache / prefix cache effectiveness (required)
We need to express cache impacts in a way that cost model can attribute “compute avoided”. Token-based units are easiest to integrate.
- runtime.kv_cache.prefill.reused_input_tokens
  - Definition: count of prompt tokens whose attention computation was skipped due to KV/prefix reuse (i.e., prefix already in cache)
  - Unit: tokens (int)
  - Constraints: MUST be <= runtime.tokens.prefill.input_total
- runtime.kv_cache.prefill.missed_input_tokens
  - Definition: prompt tokens that required fresh prefill compute (input_total - reused_input_tokens)
  - Unit: tokens (int)
- runtime.kv_cache.decode.cache_resident_rate
  - Definition: fraction of decode steps where KV pages were resident without eviction-induced recompute
  - Unit: ratio (0..1, float)
  - Rationale: we currently can’t reliably express decode recompute in tokens without more invasive instrumentation; this provides a v1 signal for “decode penalty risk” (used as a guardrail / confidence feature, not as direct cost).

C) Batch efficiency + queueing (required)
These should be emitted at the batch “execution slice” level and aggregated into request-level summaries (to avoid cardinality blowups downstream).
- runtime.batching.effective_batch_size_mean
  - Definition: mean effective batch size observed for this request across all decode steps (or prefill where applicable)
  - Unit: requests (float)
- runtime.batching.effective_batch_size_p50 / p95 (optional but strongly preferred)
  - Definition: percentiles of effective batch size during decode steps
  - Unit: requests (float)
- runtime.scheduler.queue_time_ms_total
  - Definition: total time request spent queued before execution (prefill+decode)
  - Unit: ms (int)
- runtime.scheduler.queue_time_ms_p95_step (optional)
  - Definition: p95 of per-step queue time for decode steps
  - Unit: ms (int)

D) Execution path identifiers (required, bounded cardinality)
Needed to interpret metrics across kernel paths and quant profiles; MUST be stable identifiers (no free-form strings).
- runtime.exec.attention_impl_id
  - Example values: attn_flash_v2, attn_sdpa, attn_paged_kv
- runtime.exec.quant_profile_id
  - Example values: fp16, int8_w8a16, int4_w4a16
- runtime.exec.scheduler_policy_id
  - Example values: cont_batch_v3, cont_batch_v4

Cardinality + performance constraints
- No per-token/per-layer/per-head metrics.
- No unbounded strings (model_name is ok if it’s already a bounded catalog ID; otherwise use model_id).
- All metrics must be derivable from existing scheduler + KV cache bookkeeping; no hot-path allocations.
- Target overhead: <0.5% throughput regression on standard throughput benchmark suite.

Implementation plan
1) Add counters + aggregation points
- Prefill:
  - increment input_total for normalized prompt token count
  - increment reused_input_tokens when prefix cache allows skip
- Decode:
  - increment output_total and steps_total
  - track cache resident rate via existing KV paging stats (evictions / page faults) aggregated per request
- Batching:
  - capture effective batch size for each execution slice; aggregate mean/p50/p95 in a small fixed histogram
  - capture queue time from scheduler timestamps (enqueue -> scheduled)

2) Emit via runtime metrics exporter
- Add fields to per-request runtime stats payload (the same one consumed by telemetry ingestion for token metering).
- Dual-write phase: emit old fields + new standardized ones for 1 release.

3) Telemetry integration
- Partner with Logan/Nadia to ensure naming + units match ingestion expectations.
- Add a data quality check in telemetry pipeline:
  - reused_input_tokens <= input_total
  - missed_input_tokens + reused_input_tokens == input_total
  - decode.output_total >= 0; steps_total >= output_total (if speculative can exceed)

4) Validation
- Unit tests: synthetic requests with known prefix reuse should produce expected reused/missed.
- Benchmark validation:
  - cache-off scenario (cache disabled): reused_input_tokens == 0
  - cache-on warmed: reused_input_tokens increases; observed prefill latency decreases
- Backfill / replay check (post-merge): compare new token totals vs existing token metering totals within 0.1% on sampled traffic.

Rollout
- Stage 1: canary on 1% hosted traffic in us-east; monitor exporter stability + cardinality.
- Stage 2: 25% hosted + dedicated staging.
- Stage 3: 100% hosted; then dedicated; then private packages.
- Feature flags:
  - runtime_emit_standard_cost_inputs (default off)

Acceptance criteria
- New metrics are emitted for >= 99.5% of requests on canary with no crashes.
- Data quality checks pass with <0.1% violations (violations must be explainable and documented).
- Throughput regression <0.5% on standard perf suite.
- Telemetry confirms metrics are ingested and queryable for Cost Model service.
- Cost Model team signs off that required inputs are present for v1 endpoints.

Open questions
- Do we need decode recompute expressed as “recomputed_tokens” rather than cache_resident_rate? (Would require more instrumentation; propose v2.)
- For speculative decoding: should decode.output_total reflect accepted tokens only (recommended) and steps_total reflect attempted steps? Need alignment with Nadia’s token metering definition.

Links

- Drive: runtime metric gap list: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/runtime-metric-gap-list-for-cost-model.json

Activity / comments
2026-02-06 (Omar El-Sayed)
- Drafted field list above; confirmed with Sofia that we can derive reused_input_tokens from prefix-cache bookkeeping in scheduler v4.
- Potential risk: paged KV path uses different eviction counters; may need translation to cache_resident_rate.

2026-02-10 (Nadia Rahman)
- Token metering alignment: prefill.input_total and decode.output_total must match metering totals used downstream; steps_total is fine as a separate field.
- Please ensure speculative decoding reports accepted tokens in output_total and attempted in steps_total.

2026-02-12 (Logan Wright)
- Please keep execution path IDs bounded; do not include raw kernel names.
- Add invariant check reused <= input_total in exporter before emission (drop/zero on invalid rather than poisoning pipeline).

2026-02-14 (Sofia Ivanova)
- Batch efficiency: effective_batch_size should be based on “active sequences” per decode step (excluding padded slots). We can compute this cheaply from scheduler state.

2026-02-17 (Omar El-Sayed)
- Implementation completed behind runtime_emit_standard_cost_inputs.
- Added fixed-bin histogram to compute p50/p95 effective batch size without storing all samples.
- Prepared PR: runtime export KV cache stats + prefill/decode split; requesting review from Sofia + Logan.

2026-02-18 (Allison Grant)
- Observability note: ensure we can attribute missing metrics to exporter version; include runtime_build_id in payload if already present elsewhere. Avoid adding it as a new high-cardinality label in metrics backend.

Next steps
- Land PR, enable canary, and coordinate with Telemetry team for ingestion mapping.
- After 1 week of clean canary, start dual-write deprecation plan for legacy fields (tracked under ENG-4823 follow-up).

Risks
- Telemetry lag can make cache_resident_rate appear unstable; we should avoid using it for hard cost attribution in v1 (ok as confidence/guardrail only).
- Incorrect prefill/decode split will cause visible drift in Console; ensure perf suite includes regression test for the split (tie into golden fixtures work).
